raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57096/files) against `main`.

## Summary

Implement the `minicpm5` tool-parser parity item for the Rust frontend from #44280. This updates the existing PR rather than opening a duplicate.

Add native MiniCPM5 XML-style function-call parsing and register it with Rust chat serving. Support non-streaming and streaming output, arbitrary decoded chunk boundaries, multiple calls, schema-aware parameter conversion/validation, wrapped parameters, aliases, and invalid/truncated-input fallback. Streaming emits each call ID/name once and reconstructs valid JSON arguments.

Add four real-model OpenAI E2E cases to the existing tool-use suite: single/multiple calls × synchronous/streaming responses. Reuse its model configuration and fixtures, and add a MiniCPM5 command to the existing Rust frontend tool-use CI job.

## Test Plan

Rebased onto vLLM main `ab35354c21cc3c36439e79e18070f85cfafc3af2`, addressing the merge-conflict report. Feature commit: `2f97de24b32844019fee456ccc757b313c19e9a3`; E2E commit / tested head: `48ec263c5558b91e485106cb9c7dd08e4fbe9520`.

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --lib
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat \
  --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --release -p vllm-cmd --bin vllm-rs

VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 pytest -v -s tests/tool_use/test_tool_calls.py \
  --models minicpm5 --extended -k test_minicpm5_auto_tool_calls
```

## Test Result

| Test | Tested revision / scope | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MiniCPM5 parser unit tests | Rebased head; XML parsing, chunk boundaries, schema handling, fallback | 5 passed (included below) |
| Parser regression | Rebased head, `cargo test -p vllm-parser --lib` | 462 passed |
| Chat unit regression | Rebased head, `cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib` | 333 passed, including MiniCPM5 registry test |
| Chat integration | Rebased head, `tests/chat.rs` | 17 passed |
| Cross-model HF roundtrip | Rebased head, `tests/roundtrip.rs` | 1 passed; 18 failed fetching HF model files due to connection timeouts; not counted as passed |
| Rust formatting / Clippy | Rebased head; parser/chat all targets, `-D warnings` | Passed |
| Python lint / format / diff hygiene | Rebased head; repository-configured Ruff, `git diff --check` | Passed |
| Release Rust frontend build | Rebased head, `vllm-cmd --bin vllm-rs` | Built successfully |
| Real GPU E2E before rebase | Four new pytest cases; original feature binary | 4 passed, 2 deselected, 85.36 s |
| Real GPU E2E after rebase: single call, non-streaming | Rebuilt Rust frontend + real MiniCPM5-2B / DSpark | Passed |
| Real GPU E2E after rebase: single call, streaming | Same; reconstruct JSON arguments, ID/name emitted once | Passed |
| Real GPU E2E after rebase: two calls, non-streaming | Same; unique IDs and expected city set | Passed |
| Real GPU E2E after rebase: two calls, streaming | Same; indexed deltas and `finish_reason=tool_calls` | Passed |
| Four-case post-rebase E2E aggregate | Exact committed pytest file, SHA256 `9d704048f2db8f4db8b1f923e10a3e8b99bac8654b11cf4b254a2008eecba9c8` | 4 passed, 2 deselected, 14.39 s |
| H200 / ROCm CI and broad model quality / performance | Not run locally | Pending CI / outside targeted validation |

Real GPU serving uses one NVIDIA L20, vLLM 0.29.0, BF16 MiniCPM5-2B and MiniCPM5-2B-DSpark, eager mode and seven speculative tokens. The Rust frontend is rebuilt from the rebased source; the Python engine is the installed vLLM 0.29.0 runtime, not a full Python-main engine validation. Binary SHA256: `6f8a55e37930f2c0e86e7bae207c1d0130f2ba47bbbdc0ad07b2ced45b36ae45`.

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  /path/to/MiniCPM5-2B --served-model-name MiniCPM5-2B \
  --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 2048 --enforce-eager \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/path/to/MiniCPM5-2B-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser minicpm5
```

The earlier real-model smoke passed a non-streaming weather call, streaming tool-call deltas with reconstructable JSON arguments, and two weather calls in one completion, all with `finish_reason=tool_calls`. DSpark itself is not modified by this PR. These are targeted tool-serving regressions, not broad model-quality or performance evaluations.

The local four-case run uses the committed pytest file against an independently started real service, with a live-server client fixture (`AsyncOpenAI` at localhost), not a mock engine. CI uses the existing tool-use server fixtures and the new `--models minicpm5 --extended` command. JUnit and server logs are retained. Draft pending review.

   - pytest -v -s tool_use --ignore=tool_use/mistral --models llama3.2 -k "not test_response_format_with_tool_choice_required and not test_parallel_tool_calls_false and not test_tool_call_and_choice"

   mirror:
     amd:
       label: ":amd: (MI355 DPX) Rust Frontend Tool Use"

@@ -17,6 +17,96 @@
 )
 
 
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("stream", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cities", [("Shenzhen",), ("Shenzhen", "Hangzhou")])
+async def test_minicpm5_auto_tool_calls(client, server_config, stream, cities):
+    """MiniCPM5 XML calls must become complete OpenAI tool calls in both modes."""
+    if server_config["model"] != "openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B":
+        pytest.skip("MiniCPM5-specific tool-call regression")
+
+    model = (await client.models.list()).data[0].id
+    response = await client.chat.completions.create(
+        model=model,
+        messages=[
+            {
+                "role": "system",
+                "content": (
+                    "Call get_weather once for each city requested. "
+                    "Do not answer directly. Preserve the city names exactly."
+                ),
+            },
+            {
+                "role": "user",
+                "content": f"Get the weather for {' and '.join(cities)}.",
+            },
+        ],
+        tools=[
+            {
+                "type": "function",
+                "function": {
+                    "name": "get_weather",
+                    "description": "Get current weather for one city",
+                    "parameters": {
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
+                        "required": ["city"],
+                    },
+                },
+            }
+        ],
+        tool_choice="auto",
+        temperature=0,
+        seed=SEED,
+        max_completion_tokens=192,
+        stream=stream,
+    )
+
+    calls = {}
+    finish_reasons = []
+    if stream:
+        async for chunk in response:
+            for choice in chunk.choices:
+                if choice.finish_reason is not None:
+                    finish_reasons.append(choice.finish_reason)
+                for delta in choice.delta.tool_calls or []:
+                    call = calls.setdefault(
+                        delta.index, {"id": None, "name": None, "arguments": ""}
+                    )
+                    if delta.id is not None:
+                        assert call["id"] is None
+                        call["id"] = delta.id
+                    if delta.function is not None:
+                        if delta.function.name is not None:
+                            assert call["name"] is None
+                            call["name"] = delta.function.name
+                        call["arguments"] += delta.function.arguments or ""
+    else:
+        choice = response.choices[0]
+        finish_reasons.append(choice.finish_reason)
+        assert choice.message.role == "assistant"
+        calls = {
+            index: {
+                "id": call.id,
+                "name": call.function.name,
+                "arguments": call.function.arguments,
+            }
+            for index, call in enumerate(choice.message.tool_calls or [])
+        }
+
+    assert finish_reasons == ["tool_calls"]
+    assert set(calls) == set(range(len(cities)))
+    assert len({call["id"] for call in calls.values()}) == len(cities)
+    parsed_cities = []
+    for call in calls.values():
+        assert call["id"]
+        assert call["name"] == "get_weather"
+        arguments = json.loads(call["arguments"])
+        assert set(arguments) == {"city"}
+        parsed_cities.append(arguments["city"])
+    assert sorted(parsed_cities) == sorted(cities)
+
+
